v.q: How do jobs in the same stage run?
v.w: Stages run in order, and the jobs inside one stage run at the same time.

v.q: What happens when a job in the build stage fails?
o: The next stage does not start
v.w: A stage must succeed before the next begins, unless the failed job has allow_failure.

v.q: What does a GitLab runner do?
o: Polls GitLab and runs the jobs
v.w: The server runs no jobs. A runner asks for them, so it only needs outbound access.

v.q: Which executor runs each job in a fresh container?
v.w: The Docker executor starts a new container from the image in the job, then removes it.

v.q: Which statement about the cache is true?
o: It is best effort and may be missing
It is guaranteed for later jobs
v.w: A job must still work when the cache is empty. Use artifacts for results.

v.q: Which keyword passes a JAR to the next job?
v.w: Artifacts are results uploaded by GitLab and downloaded by later jobs of the same pipeline.

v.q: What does a protected variable do?
o: Limits it to protected branches and tags
Hides it from the UI forever
v.w: A feature branch pipeline cannot read production credentials that are protected.

v.q: What is better than a stored production password?
v.w: The job exchanges a GitLab ID token with Vault or a cloud for temporary access, so nothing long-lived is stored.

Which runner tags a job needs
The cache key for a job
v.w: It avoids duplicate pipelines, for example one for the branch and one for its merge request.

v.q: What should a merge request pipeline normally NOT do?
v.w: It gives quick feedback on the change. Deployment belongs to the default branch or a release tag.

Selects the runner for a job
v.w: It turns stages into a graph, so a job does not wait for the whole previous stage.

v.q: Which setting lets a new push cancel an old pipeline?
v.w: Interruptible jobs can be cancelled when a newer pipeline makes them obsolete.

v.q: Why pin the ref of an included template?
o: A template change hits every project
It makes the YAML file shorter
It hides the template from users
v.w: Treat templates like a library: upgrade on purpose with a reviewed commit.

v.q: Which keyword inherits a hidden job such as .java-job?
v.w: Hidden jobs start with a dot and are reused with extends, so shared settings live in one place.

v.q: What does a protected environment add?
v.w: It gives four-eyes control: only listed roles may deploy, and approvals can be required.
Jobs sharing a resource group run one at a time, so deployments do not overlap.
